newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Thousands of Hutu refugees arrive at Zaire village.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Hutu refugees arrive at Zaire village.

text.p: Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees arrived at a village in east Zaire's Masisi region on Monday saying they wanted to return home, the U.N. refugee agency said.
Up to 30,000 refugees who fled camps around Goma and Bukavu in November at the start of a rebel campaign arrived at Karuba village west of Goma, UNHCR official Filippo Grandi told Reuters.
Aid workers would on Tuesday give food and water to the refugees and prepare for their journey to Rwanda by truck or on foot, Grandi said.
"We have asked the Alliance (rebels) to give them safe passage ... The people seemed in reasonable health so there shouldn't be too many problems," Grandi said.

Rebels from the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire (AFDL) have captured around a quarter of Zaire since launching their rebellion in October to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.
There was no explanation for the sudden arrival of the refugees but Tutsis and extremist Hutus are fighting a dirty ethnic war in the Masisi connected to ethnic strife in neighbouring Rwanda.

Members of the Hutu Interahamwe militias and former Rwandan army blamed for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in Rwanda in 1994 took to the hills west of Goma after rebels overran their refugee camps last year.
The area is now controlled by rebels, many of whom are Tutsi trying to secure East Zaire from the extremist Hutu threat and control more land for their cattle.
More than a million refugees fled camps in Kivu region in October and November at the start of Zaire's civil war, but more than 600,000 returned to Rwanda via Goma in November.
Since then UNHCR says it has repatriated 140,000 refugees through Kivu region.
